mail.subject: Last year’s #1 model is unranked today
paragraphs: This week in 60 seconds: MiniMax M3.1 Flash enters at #27, priced at $0.15/$0.60 per million tokens. Argon is now #5, Supported. Mercury 3 has no rank yet.
The board, scored October 20: Argon moved from #6 Estimated to #5 Supported. BenchLM says Supported means enough independent source families to stand behind the row; ranks can still move.

MiniMax M3.1 Flash launched October 19 at $0.15 input and $0.60 output per million tokens. Its benchmark rows are MiniMax's own runs. MiniMax says agentic task cost is 70% lower; BenchLM says it cannot check this claim yet.
Claude Haiku 5.5 is $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens for prompts under 100K tokens; above 100K it is $0.50/$2.50. The author summarizes the two models as within 20% on price.
Inception reports Mercury 3 generates 1,068 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs. BenchLM has no outside lab run and does not assign a score. Unranked, not low.
DeepSeek's deepseek-flash endpoint received the 1017 upgrade on October 17, according to the newsletter. This paragraph does not describe the Bailian endpoint.

From the archive: August 2025 ranks were rebuilt with that day's scoring code, which predates BenchAlign v5. The author says compare names, not scores. GPT-5 (high), ranked #1 then, is unranked in the current board.
